### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 42 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0aed950e039c6bf538750dd4791f5802170788e9` — the merge of head `d02efc885df117d23e9a8e02a30edab62d8726c2` into base `6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0aed950e039c6bf538750dd4791f5802170788e9 && git checkout 0aed950e039c6bf538750dd4791f5802170788e9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e d02efc885df117d23e9a8e02a30edab62d8726c2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e && git merge --no-ff d02efc885df117d23e9a8e02a30edab62d8726c2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31915 (Fixes #31882) · 2026-11-09T12:46Z

Head-sha: `d02efc88`

- **Form:** draft PR to `main`, landing the card under `Fixes #31882`. `Clause-②: no`: read and write results are unchanged, and only the plan changes. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Patch changeset.
- **Premise (step 0, ruling 6738355121):** on `main`, a read by parent walks the organization index or scans the table. PostgreSQL 16 at 1M rows takes 73 ms; SQLite at 200k rows takes 21 ms. With a `(col)` index both use an index search: 1.4 ms and 0.2 ms.
- **Change, scope B as ruled:** `declaredIndexSet` adds an `idx_TABLE_COL` `(col)` index for each authored single-valued `master_detail`, `lookup` and `user` column.
  - Skipped: multi-valued columns, the system columns, the tenant column, and any column a declared index already leads with.
  - The boot sync (`syncTableIndexes`, plus the rotation gate) and `os migrate plan` read the same composition, and the orphan pass sees the index as expected.
  - `indexedKeyColumns` keeps its declared composition and adds the implicit set as a third pass. The seat checked that reference types keep the default `string(255)` width whether keyed or not, so no column drift follows.
- **Pins and ablations:** 12 cases in a new file, running on SQLite and live PG 16, and no existing test changed.
  - A read by parent plans through the index.
  - An older table gains the index at the next sync, and a further sync issues no DDL.
  - An author who declares `{ fields: [col] }` later gets one index.
  - Multi-valued and system columns are skipped.
  - CONTROL: declared indexes are unchanged.
  - Each ablation is red, then restored clean.
- **CI fix on the way:** the CLI pin `generate-string-family-width.pin.test.ts` reads `indexedKeyColumns`' source text. `0e6a2a46` went red on Test Core 7/8. `d02efc88` restores the original composition and adds a third loop. The pin was red then green locally (30/30), and the five CLI files that read these sources pass 87/87.
- **Deviations accepted:**
  - The PG plan pin turns `enable_seqscan` off on a one-connection pool.
  - Rotation shards carry the declared indexes only.
  - MySQL was not measured.
  - The PG plain `CREATE INDEX` write lock is named in the changeset, about 0.5 s at 1M rows. `CONCURRENTLY` is its own card.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31915` reports NOT governed, +377/−5. K = 14 first-parent commits on `main` since the merge base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates at `d02efc88`: 67/67 exit 0. driver-sql: 4194 passed. Dogfood upgrade-harness and index-equivalence: 26/26. CI run 42615917384 is green on this head.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31882, `pm:dispatched` removed, and #31901 moved to `pm:queue`.
